candidate.proposed_behavior: Change the dimensions or storage view of an array while preserving rank; for adjustable arrays return the same array identity, while if a distinct result is returned the original array remains unchanged. Observable options include replacing contents, resizing a fill pointer, and establishing or removing displacement while preserving intermediate displaced-array identity.

positive_laws.law: If the input array is actually adjustable, ADJUST-ARRAY returns that identical array object.
positive_laws.witness: Make an adjustable vector, change its dimensions with INITIAL-ELEMENT, and check EQ between the input and result.

positive_laws.law: If the returned array is not EQ to the input, the input array is unchanged.
positive_laws.witness: Adjust a non-adjustable vector and compare the original with a pre-call copy only when the returned array differs.

positive_laws.law: An explicit FILL-POINTER of T sets the resulting vector fill pointer to its size.
positive_laws.witness: Adjust an adjustable vector to four elements with FILL-POINTER T and observe fill-pointer = 4.

positive_laws.law: DISPLACED-TO shares backing storage; mutation through the adjusted view is observed by the immediate backing array.
positive_laws.witness: Adjust an adjustable vector to be displaced to a base at offset 2, write index 0 of the result, and observe base index 2.

positive_laws.law: If A is displaced to B and B is adjusted, A remains displaced to B; the intermediate view is not flattened away.
positive_laws.witness: Create C <- B <- A, adjust B into its own storage, then verify ARRAY-DISPLACEMENT(A) still returns B and A writes are observed through B.

falsifiers: Claiming novelty solely because Common Lisp spells the operation ADJUST-ARRAY.

Treating ADJUST-ARRAY as identical to historical *REARRAY without testing returned identity, preservation of the original when a distinct result is returned, fill-pointer updates, and displacement chains.
Treating ARRAY-DISPLACEMENT (which only observes backing array plus offset) as equivalent to array adjustment.

Assuming any difference from REARRAY must automatically earn a resident: test derivability from MAKE-ARRAY, REARRAY, COPY-ARRAY, element access/update and the concurrently reviewed ARRAY-DISPLACEMENT law.
Assigning a coordinate or ratification before the owner reviews the behavioral/derivability results.

neighbors.name: MAKE-ARRAY
neighbors.relationship: Creates a new array. It does not itself implement the identity/conditional-original-preservation protocol of adjusting an existing object.

neighbors.name: REARRAY
neighbors.relationship: MacLisp operation; preserves row-major contents while redefining dimensions and fills new typed cells. This is the main differential/derivability attack.

neighbors.name: COPY-ARRAY
neighbors.relationship: Copies an array; copying alone does not express identity-preserving adjustment or displaced-view mutation.

neighbors.name: ARRAY-DISPLACEMENT
neighbors.relationship: Observation of immediate base array and offset, not the mutation/adjustment operation. Keep the PR's selection decision separate.

admission_decision.rationale: The source laws are precise and executable, but semantic independence from selected D10 REARRAY/MAKE-ARRAY has not yet been demonstrated strongly enough for selection. This tranche deliberately stops at HOLD pending the donor oracle and owner review.
admission_decision.next_gate: Run the SBCL oracle; review its output against the pinned MacLisp *REARRAY contract and active D10 neighbors. If only a composition of existing semantics remains, reject as a new root; otherwise propose a separate serialized +1 selection PR.
